title: Filtered coherent submodule surjecting at an integral generic stalk
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $\eta$ its generic point [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $F_{i(\eta)}$ is nonzero [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and is annihilated by the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,i(\eta)}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there are a coherent module $A$ and a monomorphism $f:A\to F$ such that $A$ has a coherent integral-ideal filtration [def-weil-pbc-coherent-integral-filtration] and $f_{i(\eta)}$ is surjective. No support hypothesis on $F$, cokernel assertion or support induction is required.

source.place: Tags 01YE (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible) and 01YF (lemma-coherent-filter), the generic ideal inclusion and filtration of its finite-sum source; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YF.

proof.text: Construct the local free model using maximal-ideal annihilation. Extend its specific isomorphism from a coherent ideal-sum lattice, keeping agreement and invertibility of the lattice inclusion on the same open.

The agreement and the two restricted isomorphisms make alpha invertible on that open, hence bijective on the generic stalk. Prove the generalized finite-sum vanishing lemma: a map into a pushed finite sum of ideals with zero generic stalk is zero. Compare the pushed coproduct with the biproduct of pushed ideals. For every coordinate, embed the ideal into the structure sheaf, represent a zero generic germ on a smaller open, and use injectivity of integral restrictions to kill the original section. Finite biproduct projections detect zero maps, including the empty sum. Apply this generalized lemma directly to the kernel inclusion, whose generic stalk map is zero by cancellation against the generic isomorphism. Thus alpha is mono. All these steps are proved in Lean with no new hole; no duplicate rank-one theorem is declared.
If I=0, or if r=0, the pushed finite sum and its generic stalk are zero. Surjectivity contradicts hx. Thus I is nonzero and r is positive.

Closed Z is Noetherian. Coherence of I gives quasi-coherence; qcqs pushforward preserves it. A summand injects into the finite sum and then into F. Therefore the pushed ideal is coherent by the quasi-coherent submodule criterion, without using the finite-pushforward-coherence module.

Induct on r using the zero-sum filtration and the pushforward successor-sum comparison. At the successor step append the coherent pushed ideal using Z,i,I as the final integral quotient witness. The resulting filtration implies coherence of its whole source, by its top endpoint and coherence invariant under isomorphism. Return that source, alpha, its proved mono property and generic surjectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_generic_filtered_source
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (hx : ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint Z))))
    (hkill : ∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal
      (X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint Z))),
      ∀ m : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint Z))).obj F, a • m = 0) :
    ∃ (A : X.Modules) (f : A ⟶ F), Mono f ∧
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace A ∧ HasCoherentIntegralFiltration A ∧
      Function.Surjective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint Z))).map f)
